mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings prospects.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS shows a month-over-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 8.0%, it signals a tightening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 8.0% but 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days as corporate profits rise.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO > 100 and RSAFS > 400000) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a low interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%), a month-over-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month in the low-rate regime but 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects stronger manufacturing activity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate outlook.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows a month-over-month increase but 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 650.0 thousand units, it signals a strengthening housing market that drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days due to increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: HOUST > 650.0 but 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate is positive but 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
